If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Paul left Titus with a charge: “For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.” Set in order the things that are lacking.

So when you hear people say rank ain't nothing: rank is important for structure's sake. The elders were appointed and set in order, and the body of Christ runs on that structure.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.” That is why people have left the truth of the word of God to follow fables. Christmas is a fable. All of those are fables, meaning lies, story-told lies, with symbolic meanings in the stories: Santa Claus and his blackened helper, Santa with his horse in the Netherlands and his flying reindeer here, Rudolph and the fairy dust. Our people have celebrated this foolishness for a long time.

Titus gives the warning: “Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.” Don’t give heed to them. Christmas and all these things are commandments of men, and they turn you from the truth.

That is why you have people online saying it is not wrong to celebrate Christmas, it is in your heart, it is how you feel, and all that crap. It is turning you from the truth of God. Some try to figure it out: we agree his birthday is not December 25th, so we can make up another day. That is what they do, but it always comes back to December 25th. It is still a fable and a commandment of men, and Paul told Timothy the people would turn away their ears from the truth to follow it.

precepts.text: Read by the teacher as a prophecy of the birth of Christ.
precepts.point: Christ was not born on December 25.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Not giving heed to Jewish fables.” A fable is a lie, and it says Jewish because it pertains to the Jews. Christ was a Jew, and there is a lie being told that he was born on December 25th. That is a Jewish fable. Christmas goes back into slavery and into paganism too, and it turns you away from the truth of serving God. It has nothing to do with Christ.

Luke tells what happened: “the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger.” Her firstborn, meaning she had many sons; the Catholic Church says Mary was a virgin who never had sex, but she brought forth her firstborn. And before he was put in the manger, the prophecy in the Song of Solomon shows where he was born: “Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth.”

So Mary had Christ under an apple tree, and after she gave birth to him there, she took him to the manger, “because there was no room for them in the inn.” Christ was not born in the manger. A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime they are not out there; they go in the barn to stay warm.

Why was there no room in the inn, the hotel? “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.” Everybody came up to Jerusalem at that time and the inns were full, because it was the Passover. Christ was born in the springtime, not in the winter.

That is how the scripture kills the fable. Stop listening to Santa Claus, aka Pope Nicholas, St. Nicholas. Don’t give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you from the truth: Christ was not born on December 25th.

precepts.text: Things left wanting are to be set in order, which is the work of restoring the house to its right order that this chapter puts into a decree.
precepts.point: This order, that every man should bear rule in his own house, is set up in the Bible for the man, and it is the very order the Most High established that the societies of the earth keep reversing.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

precepts.why:
“the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the word of Memucan”. Letters went “into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house”. What Vashti did had left something wanting in every house of the kingdom, and the decree is the setting of it back in order.

That is the very work Paul left Titus in Crete to do: “that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city”. Where things are wanting, they are not left as they are; they are set in order. The house has a right order, and restoring it is a work that has to be done and published.

The order that “every man should bear rule in his own house” is set up in the Bible for the man. It is the order the Most High established, and it is the very order the societies of the earth keep reversing. This chapter puts the restoring of it into a decree, published in the language of every people.

precepts.point: Like Christ saying he that has ears let him hear, everyone has ears, but only the one with understanding truly hears the wisdom coming out.

note.label: Proverbs 8: Wisdom Crieth in the Streets and Christ Set Up from Everlasting

precepts.why:
“All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing froward or perverse in them. They are all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.” Wisdom's words have nothing froward or perverse in them, yet they are only plain and right to some.

Paul shows why: “Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.” Unto the pure all things are pure, but unto the defiled nothing is pure, even their mind and conscience being defiled. The same right words come to two kinds of hearers, and the defiled mind cannot find them right.

Everyone has ears, but only the one with understanding truly hears the wisdom coming out. The pure understand her; the defiled and unbelieving find nothing pure even in words that are all in righteousness.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Titus was an elder of the highest rank. Paul wrote “To Titus, mine own son after the common faith”, and charged him, “For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.”

A man Paul called his own son, who ordained elders in every city, who had a book written after him, yet fell away through the doctrines of circumcision and animal sacrifice. That is how strong the false brethren's bondage was, and if Titus could fall, anybody could fall.

It even goes for today. Go to any other nation and you see order, structure, organization. “That thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city”: elders are officers, judges, counsellors. The ranking system.

For those who say that’s not the New Testament: “That thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city”: to ordain an elder means there must be a ranking system. Bishops, deacons and captains are elders. The Mormons ride around on bicycles with Elder on their name tags and nobody has a problem with that, but when our people set up rank and structure, it’s evil.
